minutes.headline: Committee heard the FY22 final recommended budget (2.5% increase) and posted seven grant-funded stipend curriculum positions; budget vote set for March 17.
minutes.summary: The meeting covered the superintendent's report on the state's push for full in-person elementary return, the superintendent award, and an iReady/IXL assessment report. The committee voted to approve seven stipended curriculum leader positions funded by Title grants, approved the Keystone Collaborative amendment adding Narragansett, and waived first read of two policies. The superintendent presented the final recommended FY22 budget, with questions on non-personnel costs and sustainability of grant-funded positions; a vote is planned March 17.

budget_items.what_was_said: Positions not in the local or grant budget will be funded from Title I and Title II grant money, prorated by hire date, and also appear in the FY22 budget as a pilot.
Recommended increase compared with prior years' increases; includes contractual increases, step, longevity, and a salary reserve for bargaining.
Non-personnel falls because health insurance decreased and a premium holiday month saves money; the town is building a stabilization fund to cushion FY23.
New positions funded partly by local budget, revolving accounts, and ESSER/special education grants; some offset by eliminated positions.
Governor's figure is based on October 1 enrollment, which dropped, so an adjustment is possible; delegation asked to consider hold harmless.

what_happened.line: The superintendent presented the final recommended FY22 school budget, a 2.5% increase as headlined in the minutes; the committee is to vote on it March 17.
The committee voted 5-0 to post seven stipended curriculum coordinator positions paid from Title I and Title II grants, also shown in the FY22 budget as a pilot.
Members asked about non-personnel costs and about sustaining grant-funded positions; health insurance and a premium holiday month lower the non-personnel line.
Chapter 70 aid may be adjusted because October 1 enrollment fell; the delegation was asked to consider hold harmless.
The committee voted 5-0 to add Narragansett to the Keystone Collaborative agreement, and the 2021-22 school calendar vote was deferred for parent feedback.

why_it_matters: The March 17 vote sets the school budget the town is asked to fund, and state aid that depends on enrollment could still change what the town budget, mostly taxes, has to cover.
Seven new positions paid from temporary Title grants raise the question of who pays for them when the grants end, which can show up later as a cost on the local school budget.
